title: Benefit Analysis of a Supplementary Virtual Reality-Based Training Application During the Early Rehabilitation Phase Following Ischemic Stroke in Patients with Upper Limb Motor Impairment
summary:
A stroke is the leading cause of permanent disability in adulthood. In many cases, depending on the location of the stroke in the brain, patients experience hemiparesis, which can significantly impair their daily activities and quality of life. Early and regular rehabilitation has been shown to offer a good prognosis for regaining motor functions that were initially lost.
In this study, we aim to investigate the feasibility and effectiveness of a new virtual reality-based training therapy in the acute treatment setting of a stroke unit. At the same time, we seek to evaluate the impact of this therapy on recovery following a stroke.
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive conventional standard treatment on a stroke unit, consisting of physiotherapy, speech and language therapy, and occupational therapy. In addition, one group will receive an intervention using a VR headset over a period of up to five days. This intervention is intended to take place at least twice and up to three times daily, with each session lasting 10 minutes.
Depending on the severity of their impairment, patients will follow a predefined therapy programme that can be adapted to their individual needs, abilities, and challenges through different levels of difficulty.
The study aims to determine the extent to which this supplementary form of therapy can improve motor function. The intended effects will be assessed using various clinical outcome scores.
This benefit analysis will be complemented by satisfaction surveys involving both therapists and patients to evaluate the acceptance and tolerability of the VR application in everyday clinical practice.

interventions.name:
This is a monocentric, prospective, randomized, controlled interventional study conducted on the Stroke Unit of Kiel University Hospital.
Upon admission, the NIHSS, pre-stroke mRS, mRS, and symptom onset time will be recorded. Within 72 hours of symptom onset, patients will be screened by the ward
Control group without VR therapy; standard care remains unchanged. The respective assessments and measurements will be performed in both groups to ensure comparability.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients aged 18 years or older with an acute ischemic stroke who are undergoing acute stroke treatment as part of the comprehensive stroke unit care programme or subsequent inpatient care, and who present with motor impairments of the upper extremity.
The target population comprises patients who are capable of providing informed consent, admitted as inpatients to Kiel University Hospital (UKSH Kiel), and presenting with mild to moderate impairment of upper extremity motor function.
Prerequisites include adequate trunk stability, motor paresis of one arm with a muscle strength grade of 2 on the Medical Research Council (MRC) scale, a total NIHSS score of ≤ 5 points, and a score of no more than 9 on the Apraxia Screen of TULIA (AST).
The intervention will commence within 72 hours of symptom onset and will end after a maximum of five days.
As part of the study, an additional follow-up visit will take place 90 days after the initial stroke, for which written consent must be obtained.
Patients should have comparable levels of motor impairment and receive comparable physiotherapy and occupational therapy care.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients will be excluded if they have uncontrolled vital functions, significant visual impairments that interfere with the use of the VR headset display, open skin lesions, swelling or severe pain in the head, face or extremities, or an acute migraine attack.
Further study-related exclusion criteria include immobility; dizziness and/or nausea, where applicable; insufficient focal neurological impairment (without relevance to activities of daily living) or no impairment (e.g. following acute treatment); severe impairment (higher-grade paresis, MRC muscle strength grade ≤ 2) (NIHSS > 5); aphasia and apraxia that impair comprehension (TULIA < 5); severe delirium; neglect; if more than 72 hours have elapsed since symptom onset at the time of screening as part of the medical assessment; lack of informed consent.
The following are considered relative exclusion criteria:
- Pre-existing neurological conditions associated with cognitive or motor impairments
- Severe dyskinesia
- Epilepsy (particularly photosensitive epilepsy)
- Hemianopia
- Spasticity
- Acute exacerbations of neurodegenerative or inflammatory diseases of the central nervous system
- Comorbidities that may interfere with the therapy
- Fractures
- Shoulder joint (sub)luxations
- Severe pain in the head, face or extremities
- Cochlear implant
- Ventriculoperitoneal shunt
